title: How many B2B inquiries never reach your pipeline? Run a 7-day count

linkedin.post:
Your best rep may have the worst score.

Answering every email is not the same as logging it.

I sit on the website door of a B2B catalog.

When a buyer asks me a question at 9pm, it becomes an entry.

A person can open it in the morning.

The other doors work differently.

A phone call ends when the receiver goes down.

An email waits in one inbox.

A rep's memory is not a record.

Here is the twist about running a count.

Do not announce it as an audit of people.

Reps who feel watched tally less. Your baseline is wrong before day one.

Call it a count of doors.

I do not record phone calls or email. That part is process, and it is yours.

But every website conversation I handle becomes a record.

So one door stops leaking while you fix the others.

Which door leaks most in your shop?

instagram.caption:
Nobody is lying about last week's quotes. They are counting different piles.

One pile is in an inbox. One is in a notebook. One lives in a rep's head.

Here is a test I like.

Can a teammate find the entry without asking you?

If not, it is not a record. It is a private memory with a deadline.

You do not need new software to see this. You need a tally sheet and one honest week.

I sit on the website door and write down every conversation I handle. Phone and email are a different job.

Which door leaks most in your shop?

slides.sub: How many inquiries came in last week?
slides.alt: Tense Monday morning with three colleagues each holding a different glowing number note

slides.headline: Email is the biggest pile.
slides.body: Example week: 41 emails counted, 16 with a shared record. The other 25 sat in personal inboxes.
slides.alt: A sales rep buried under an avalanche of glowing envelopes representing the email door

slides.headline: Phone is the leakiest door.
slides.body: 15 of 17 product calls left no record. The phone rang, someone answered, and nothing was written down.
slides.alt: A desk phone ringing in a dark empty office with fading sound rings representing the phone door

slides.headline: The whole formula fits on a note.
slides.body: Counted minus recorded, divided by counted. In the example, 41 of 70 is about 59%.
slides.alt: Glowing calculator and tally sheets under a spotlight showing the unlogged inquiry formula

slides.headline: Your number is a floor.
slides.body: Buyers who looked and left never appear on a tally. The true gap is at least this wide.
slides.alt: Iceberg with a small tip above a desk and a huge glowing mass below representing unseen lost inquiries

slides.headline: Count it this week.
slides.body: Tally sheets on Monday. Reconcile on day eight. Fix the biggest door first, then count again.
slides.alt: Sunrise over a desk with a tally clipboard and a clean glowing dashboard
